canonical_data: application-held message histories and UI message streams, typed tool definitions and runtime context, serializable harness session resume state, and workflow step state when the durable agent is used
current_repo_note: GitHub reports no recognised licence because the root LICENSE file is the short Apache-2.0 notice rather than the full text; all 80 package manifests declare Apache-2.0, and one vendored schema converter carries its own ISC file.
strengths: One provider specification puts more than fifty first-party model and media packages, an OpenAI-compatible adapter, an MCP client, and LangChain and LlamaIndex bridges behind the same typed calls, so the agent loop is written once and the backend swapped

Tool approval is a first-class part of the loop: per-tool or whole-call rules return approved, denied, or ask-the-user, can change per request, and can be moved out of code into Open Policy Agent policies that see the run's full message history

The harness layer runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, fx, and five more coding agents through the same generate and stream interface, merging their built-in tools with host-executed ones and giving sessions detach, stop, and resume states
weaknesses: The tool-loop agent runs wholly in memory and loses its progress on a crash; the durable agent that fixes this depends on a workflow runtime published under a beta tag

The harness packages are labelled experimental with breaking changes expected, every harness must run in a sandbox, and the only provider that can host the bridge-backed agents is Vercel's managed sandbox
Once a telemetry integration is registered, every call records prompts and outputs by default, so keeping content out of a tracing backend is an opt-out the application has to remember
why_it_matters: The most widely adopted TypeScript agent toolkit, and the first framework to treat other vendors' finished coding agents as swappable backends the way it already treats models.
